question: Find the intervals of increase and decrease of $f(x)=\sin x+\cos x$ on $[0,2\pi]$.
explanation:
First derivative
$$f'(x)=\cos x-\sin x$$
Critical values
Setting $f'(x)=0$,
$$\cos x=\sin x\Rightarrow\tan x=1$$
In $[0,2\pi]$, this gives
$$x=\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}$$
Positive derivative intervals
On $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ and $\left(\frac{5\pi}{4},2\pi\right)$, $\cos x-\sin x>0$. Hence, $f$ is increasing.
Negative derivative interval
On $\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)$, $\cos x-\sin x<0$. Hence, $f$ is decreasing.
Conclusion
The increasing intervals are $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\cup\left(\frac{5\pi}{4},2\pi\right)$, and the decreasing interval is $\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)$.

options.B: Increasing on $\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)$ and decreasing on the remaining intervals
